G01: The default rule bans generative AI on graded work (or on all work) in the course or unit.
G02: The default rule allows, welcomes, encourages, or expects generative AI use.
G03: AI is discouraged or not recommended, but not formally prohibited.
G04: Whether AI is allowed is decided per instructor, per assignment, or per activity rather than by one rule.
G05: The policy defines named tiers, levels, colors, or categories of permitted AI use (e.g. no AI / limited / open), or a table of uses per assessment.
G06: States what applies when a syllabus or assignment says nothing about AI (e.g. 'unless explicitly allowed, AI is prohibited').
G07: Rules that cover AI built into editors and IDEs (Copilot, Cursor, autocomplete), operating systems, browsers, or autonomous coding agents, including requiring students to disable them.
G08: AI permission changes over the course: forbidden early, allowed later once fundamentals are mastered or in later projects or advanced courses.
G09: Instructors or departments must state AI expectations in the syllabus or assignment instructions.
G10: Students who are unsure whether a use is allowed should ask the instructor first, or err on the side of not using AI.
G11: One course's AI permissions do not carry over to other courses or assignments.
G12: AI may be used like a tutor or search engine to understand concepts, lecture material, or general questions, not to produce graded answers.
G13: AI may be used to explain error messages, help debug, or clarify syntax.
G14: AI may be used to generate practice problems, study guides, summaries, reviews, or self-checks of knowledge.
G15: AI may be used for brainstorming, idea generation, or exploring alternative approaches.
G16: Students may submit or use AI-generated code under explicit conditions (small snippets, line or percentage caps, cited, specific projects, or freely).
G17: The course or university provides its own sanctioned AI tool (a course chatbot, tutor bot, or licensed assistant), sometimes the only AI allowed.
G18: Specific rules for AI in prose and writing (reports, essays, comments, grammar or translation tools), separate from code.
G19: Students may not have AI generate the code, solutions, text, or answers they submit as their own.
G20: Students may not paste or upload assignment specifications, questions, their own code, or the codebase into an AI tool.
G21: Students may not use AI to debug, fix, proofread, reformat, or check graded work.
G22: No AI on exams, quizzes, tests, or in-class assessments; closed-device rules during exams.
G23: Keep AI conversations separate from the work: close the AI before writing, never copy-paste from it, never have both open, or use only browser chat interfaces.
G24: Students must disclose, acknowledge, or cite any AI use in their submission (a statement or citation).
G25: Citations of AI must include specific details such as the tool or model, the exact prompt, the output, or the date.
G26: Students must keep and submit full transcripts, chat logs, journals, drafts, or reflections on their AI use.
G27: AI-derived code must be marked at the exact place it is used (code comments, README, acknowledgments file, top of file).
G28: How disclosure affects grading or integrity: disclosed use is not penalized, or failure to disclose is itself the violation (or, conversely, disclosed use is still penalized).
G29: Students are responsible for and must own all work they submit; submitted work must be their own.
G30: Students must understand and be able to explain or defend every line and part of what they submit.
G31: AI output can be wrong, biased, or hallucinated; students must verify and critically evaluate it.
G32: Students should remain the primary thinker and decision-maker; AI must not replace their thinking.
G33: Assessment weight shifts toward proctored, in-class, or unassisted evaluation because of AI.
G34: Understanding is checked through code reviews, interviews, oral exams, demos, or meetings where students explain their work.
G35: Assignments, grading schemes, or course structure are redesigned around AI (e.g. two-pass submissions, grading on process or hours, baselines for declared AI use).
G36: Unauthorized or improper AI use is classified as academic misconduct, plagiarism, or cheating and handled by integrity processes.
G37: Specific penalties for AI misuse are stated (zero, negative score, letter-grade reduction, course failure, escalation by offense).
G38: Students can self-report, withdraw a submission, or come forward within a window for reduced consequences.
G39: AI detectors are unreliable or will not be used or relied upon as proof.
G40: Similarity checking, plagiarism software, AI-detection tools, commit histories, or activity logs are used to identify misuse.
G41: AI use is limited because doing the work yourself builds skill; outsourcing practice undermines learning.
G42: Beginners and foundational courses especially need to learn fundamentals without AI; novices cannot judge AI output.
G43: Relying on AI creates a false sense of mastery that is exposed on exams or later work.
G44: Learning to use AI effectively is a professional skill employers expect; courses teach or demonstrate AI use.
G45: AI is treated like a human collaborator, peer, or outside source under existing collaboration or citation rules.
G46: Grades must be assigned by human instructors; AI will not grade or determine grades.
G47: Instructors disclose or describe their own use of AI (in grading, feedback, demos, or communication) to students, or commit to limits on it.
G48: Course materials created with AI are disclosed and reviewed by instructors.
G49: Students may not upload course materials, assignment descriptions, or protected works into AI tools.
G50: Protect personal and confidential data; AI tools store prompts; prefer university-vetted or licensed tools.
G51: Equity and access: AI is optional or not required, free access is provided, paid tools are not required, accommodations and alternatives exist.
G52: Copyright, licensing, terms of use, and ownership of AI inputs and outputs.
G53: Ethical, bias, labor, and environmental concerns about AI.
G54: The policy is provisional and will be revisited, revised, or updated; feedback is invited.
G55: Evidence or data about how AI use affects student learning or performance is collected or cited.
